rationale: Security engineers and developers who need SSH-based text signing are a very small, technically sophisticated niche that skews strongly toward building their own open-source solution rather than paying for a GUI utility. Willingness to pay is low — KGPG and Kleopatra, the reference tools mentioned, are free; there is no demonstrated market for paid SSH signing GUIs. The problem is also infrequent (signing arbitrary text is not a daily workflow for most), and reaching enough buyers to generate meaningful revenue is structurally difficult. Additionally, the solution has non-trivial security surface area (handling SSH keys requires careful implementation), which raises build complexity and liability risk for a solo operator.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable as a paid micro-service. The niche is too small, users expect free tools, and the security-sensitive nature of SSH key handling adds complexity and risk that is inappropriate for a lightweight Claude-powered service operated solo. Drop this candidate.
notes: Fails willingness_to_pay build gate (score 3, floor 5), buyer_clarity build gate (score 5, floor 6), and buildability_with_ai build gate (score 4, floor 6). Dropped on total score (4.0 < 5.5 validate threshold).
